name: logic-date-integrity
title: Logic and date integrity
description: Checks that the stored dates of a P6 project follow from its logic, durations and schedule options: this server's CPM engine against the last F9, the activities whose dates differ with their probable cause, and the schedule options in force (read only). Use before pressing F9 on an imported update, or when the user asks whether the submitted dates can be trusted.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

template:
Logic and date integrity of project {project}: do the stored dates follow from the stored logic, durations and schedule options? This server's CPM engine recomputes the schedule and compares it with the last F9; the report lists the activities that differ and the options in force. Read only: nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=15): the engine against the last F9: match rates, activities that differ, rules.
2. so = p6_schedule_options(project="{project}"): schedule options stored for the project and the lag calendar.

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The two fixed sentences of report.md (run it before F9; ask for a reschedule when not trusted) are written
  as they are, in the user's language: add no other advice.
- Run this skill on an imported update before pressing F9: F9 recomputes the dates and the submitted ones
  are lost.

files.text:
# Logic and date integrity of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

Run this check before pressing F9 on an imported update, because F9 overwrites the submitted dates.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. The stored dates are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9), so differences are expected.
[end if]

## Engine against the last F9

- Open activities: {n_open}; match rate {match_rate} (early and late dates and total float the same); differing: {n_open_bad}.
- Completed activities: {n_done}; match rate {match_done} (early dates the same); differing: {n_done_bad}.
- Project finish: engine {finish_engine}, last F9 {finish_stored}.
- Trusted (match rate at least 0.99): {trusted}. Engine version {engine_version}.

[if not: trusted]
The stored dates do not all follow from the stored logic, durations and options: ask for a reschedule with these options and a resubmission, or an explanation of the mismatches.
[end if]

## Activities whose stored dates differ

[table: mismatched]

## What the engine models

{rules}

## Schedule options in force

Stored in: {opt_source}. Calendar of the lags: {lag_rule}. Options the project does not store take P6's defaults, which are not listed.

[table: options]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_cpm_validate says the project has no data date or that the network has a loop: repeat its message and
  stop (P6 cannot schedule a loop either).

## Warnings (fixed wording in report.md)

- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning; the probable cause of every row then says the project was
  edited since its last F9.
- trusted is false (or the match rate is n/a): keep the sentence asking for a reschedule and a resubmission,
  or an explanation of the mismatches.
- The sentence on running this check before F9 is always kept.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The match rates are the fields match_rate and match_rate_completed, never a share you worked out from the
  counts.
- The activities table keeps the rows in the order returned and stops at 15; when cv has more pages
  (next_offset not null) it ends with "Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities that differ.",
  both numbers copied from cv.
- The options table lists the options as returned (at most 40), the value as stored.
- Activities are written "Activity ID - name".
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Logic and date integrity

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. cv = p6_cpm_validate(project="{project}", limit=15): the engine against the last F9: match rates, activities that differ, rules.
2. so = p6_schedule_options(project="{project}"): schedule options stored for the project and the lag calendar.

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given

## Units

- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | cv.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |
| last_f9 | cv.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | cv.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | changed by this server after the last F9 |
| match_rate | cv.match_rate |  | n2 | n/a | share of open activities with the same early and late dates and total float (1.00 = all) |
| match_done | cv.match_rate_completed |  | n2 | n/a | share of completed activities with the same early dates |
| trusted | cv.trusted |  | flag | n/a | match rate at least 0.99 |
| n_open | cv.counts.open | count | int | n/a | open activities |
| n_open_bad | cv.counts.open_mismatched | count | int | n/a | open activities that differ |
| n_done | cv.counts.completed | count | int | n/a | completed activities |
| n_done_bad | cv.counts.completed_mismatched | count | int | n/a | completed activities whose early dates differ |
| finish_engine | cv.project_finish.engine |  | datetime | n/a | project finish computed by the engine |
| finish_stored | cv.project_finish.stored |  | datetime | n/a | project finish of the last F9 |
| rules | cv.rules |  | text | n/a | what the engine models |
| engine_version | cv.engine_version |  | int | n/a | version of the engine's date and float rules |
| opt_source | so.db_source |  | text | n/a | where the options are stored |
| lag_rule | so.lag_rule.db_effective |  | text | n/a | calendar of the lags |

## Table mismatched

Open activities first, then completed ones, by Activity ID.

Rows: cv.rows, in the order returned, at most 15.
When cv.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities that differ. (returned and total of cv).
No rows: write 'No activity differs: every stored date follows from the logic.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Differences (stored, engine) | differences_text |  | text | n/a |  |
| Probable cause | probable_cause |  | text | n/a |  |

## Table options

Options stored in the database, as P6 names them.

Rows: so.options, in the order returned, at most 40 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 40 items, add the line: Only the first 40 options are shown.
No rows: write 'No schedule option is stored for this project.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Option | option |  | text | n/a |  |
| Value | db |  | text | not stored |  |

# Logic and date integrity of DEMO-SS225

Data date 2026-10-26, last schedule run (F9) 2026-10-26 17:30. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

Run this check before pressing F9 on an imported update, because F9 overwrites the submitted dates.

## Engine against the last F9

- Open activities: 75; match rate 1.00 (early and late dates and total float the same); differing: 0.
- Completed activities: 139; match rate 1.00 (early dates the same); differing: 0.
- Project finish: engine 2027-10-05 17:00, last F9 2027-10-05 17:00.
- Trusted (match rate at least 0.99): yes. Engine version 1.

## Activities whose stored dates differ

No activity differs: every stored date follows from the logic.

## What the engine models

retained logic placing every status (lag between two completed activities ignored), lag elapsed before the data date dropped, calendars per activity, lag rule calendar, must finish date for open ends, total float per sched_float_type; LOE, WBS summary, ALAP approximated; leveling not modelled

## Schedule options in force

Stored in: PROJPROP scheduling. Calendar of the lags: rcal_Predecessor. Options the project does not store take P6's defaults, which are not listed.

|-|-|
| enable_multiple_longest_path_calc | Y |
| key_activity_for_multiple_longest_paths | (none) |
| level_all_rsrc_flag | Y |
| level_float_thrs_cnt | 0 |
| level_keep_sched_date_flag | Y |
| level_outer_assign_flag | N |
| level_outer_assign_priority | 1 |
| level_over_alloc_pct | 0.0 |
| level_within_float_flag | N |
| limit_multiple_longest_path_calc | Y |
| max_multiple_longest_path | 5 |
| sched_calendar_on_relationship_lag | rcal_Predecessor |
| sched_float_type | FT_FF |
| sched_lag_early_start_flag | Y |
| sched_open_critical_flag | N |
| sched_outer_depend_type | SD_Both |
| sched_progress_override | N |
| sched_retained_logic | Y |
| sched_setplantoforecast | N |
| sched_use_expect_end_flag | Y |
| sched_use_project_end_date_for_float | Y |
| use_total_float_multiple_longest_paths | Y |
| levelprioritylist | priority_type:ASC |
